name: nng
why: Brokerless messaging with scalability protocols is a doorway into messaging patterns, though it reads as a generic library.

brief.what_it_is: NNG is a lightweight C library for brokerless messaging. Applications link against it and use its API to send and receive messages over sockets that implement common messaging patterns such as publish/subscribe, RPC-style request/reply, and service discovery. It handles connection management, retries, and similar plumbing so the application code can focus on its own logic. The page does not describe a command-line tool beyond the executable name nngcat, which the brew metadata lists.
brief.why_it_exists: The homepage presents NNG as the successor to nanomsg, and to some extent ZeroMQ, that keeps a simple API for recurring messaging problems and takes the design further. It also says the project offers wire and API compatibility with nanomsg, so existing nanomsg and mangos applications can interoperate with NNG applications.
brief.how_it_works: The homepage says NNG scales out across cores with a bespoke asynchronous I/O framework that uses thread pools. It avoids tying itself to file descriptors and avoids interlocking state machines, which it credits for making new protocols and transports easier to add; the TLS and ZeroTier transports are given as examples. Optional separation of protocol context and state from sockets is offered for concurrent applications.

brief.install_notes: Building needs a C99-compatible compiler and CMake 3.13 or newer. The page recommends the Ninja build system (pass -G Ninja to CMake). TLS support additionally requires mbedTLS, with details in docs/BUILD_TLS.md in the repository. The homepage's Quick Start covers only the Linux/UNIX build path; no Windows or macOS steps are shown. Homebrew install is the route for the nngcat executable.
brief.standout: The homepage stresses reliability in a way that is unusual for a messaging library: it says every error case is considered and the library is designed to avoid crashing except in cases of gross developer error. It also claims the separation of protocol state from sockets makes concurrent applications much simpler, and that the library is hardened for use on a hostile Internet.
brief.status: unknown. The homepage shows no release version, release date, or last-commit date, and I did not follow links to the repository or changelog to check. The page does list 'Used By' and 'Sponsors' sections, but their contents did not come through as text.
brief.caveats: TLS needs a separate mbedTLS dependency. The Quick Start shows only the Linux/UNIX path. The homepage lists supported platforms as Linux, macOS, Windows (Vista or better), illumos, Solaris, FreeBSD, Android, and iOS, and says other POSIX systems are untested. The scout note calls it a generic library, and the homepage itself describes it in general terms with few concrete examples.
quotes: NNG, like its predecessors nanomsg (and to some extent ZeroMQ), is a lightweight, broker-less library, offering a simple API to solve common recurring messaging problems
The API frees the programmer from worrying about details like connection management, retries, and other common considerations, so that they can focus on the application instead of the plumbing.
it is designed to avoid crashing except in cases of gross developer error.
